lede: A nobleman of Quraysh, come to Madinah to bargain for the prisoners of Badr, stood outside the mosque at sunset and heard this surah. When it reached its run of questions — were they created from nothing, or are they the creators? — he said his heart nearly took flight. It was the first time faith settled in it.

names.name: al-Ṭūr
names.note: After the oath it opens with: the mountain on which Allah spoke to Mūsā. The Companions called it by this name — “I heard the Prophet ﷺ recite al-Ṭūr in the sunset prayer” (al-Bukhārī 765).

revelation.detail: It is Makkan in the saying of all: Ibn al-Jawzī and al-Qurṭubī both record the agreement. The traditional order places it seventy-sixth.

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ الطُّورِ وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّها بِإجْماعِهِمْ
عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ جُبَير بْنِ مُطْعِمٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ: سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ يَقْرَأُ فِي الْمَغْرِبِ بِالطُّورِ، فَمَا سَمِعْتُ أَحَدًا أَحْسَنَ صَوْتًا -أَوْ قِرَاءَةً-مِنْهُ

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ الضُّرَيْسِ، والنَّحّاسُ، وابْنُ مَرْدُويَهْ، والبَيْهَقِيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ ”الطُّورِ“ بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by Ibn al-Ḍurays, al-Naḥḥās, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī.

attested.quote: هي مَكِّيَّةٌ، قالَ القُرْطُبِيُّ: في قَوْلِ الجَمِيعِ

setting: No occasion is reported for its revelation. What is recorded is the effect it had on one of its hearers. Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim was the son of one of the chief men of Makkah. After Badr he was sent to Madinah to negotiate for the captives, and arrived as the Prophet ﷺ was leading the sunset prayer.

“I heard the Prophet ﷺ reciting al-Ṭūr in the sunset prayer,” he said. “When he reached this ayah — ‘Or were they created by nothing, or are they themselves the creators? Or did they create the heavens and the earth? No, they have no certainty. Or do they possess the treasuries of your Lord, or are they the ones in control?’ — my heart almost flew.” In another narration: “And that was when faith first settled in my heart.” He was still an idolater. He accepted Islam some years later.

Those ayat are the centre of the surah: a volley of some fifteen questions, each beginning with “or”, that goes through every position a denier could take and leaves none standing. Is he a soothsayer? A poet whose death they can wait for? Did he make it up — then let them produce a discourse like it. Do they have a ladder by which they listen to the heavens? Does Allah have daughters while they have sons? Do they have another god?

Around that centre the surah sets its certainties: five oaths that the punishment will fall, the Fire into which the deniers are driven, and the people of the Garden, who turn to one another and remember how, among their families in the world, they had been afraid.
aim: To refute the doubts of the deniers by setting out proofs and evidence — compelling them to yield and submit.
themes: The people of the Garden and their families

outline.title: Five oaths
outline.summary: By the Mount; by a Book inscribed on parchment unrolled; by the House frequented; by the canopy raised high; by the sea set aflame: the punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass. There is none to avert it.

outline.title: The Day
outline.summary: The Day the sky heaves and the mountains move. Woe that Day to the deniers, who play in their idle talk — the Day they are thrust into the fire of Hell: “This is the Fire you used to deny. Is this magic, then, or do you not see? Burn in it; be patient or impatient, it is the same for you.”

outline.title: The people of the Garden
outline.summary: The mindful will be in gardens and delight, reclining on ranged couches. Those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith — We shall join their offspring to them, and take nothing from their own deeds; every person is in pledge for what he earned. They turn to one another, asking: “We used to be fearful, before, among our families. So Allah was gracious to us and saved us from the scorching wind. We used to call upon Him; He is the Kind, the Merciful.”

outline.title: The questions
outline.summary: So remind: by your Lord’s favour you are neither a soothsayer nor a madman. Or do they say, “A poet — we await for him some turn of fate”? Or “He has invented it”? Then let them bring a discourse like it. Or were they created from nothing, or are they the creators? Did they create the heavens and the earth? Do they hold the treasuries of your Lord? Have they a ladder to listen by? Has He daughters, while you have sons? Do you ask them for a wage? Do they possess the unseen? Do they intend a plot? Or have they a god other than Allah?

outline.title: Leave them, and be patient
outline.summary: If they saw a piece of the sky falling they would say, “Clouds, heaped up.” So leave them until they meet their Day. Be patient for the decision of your Lord, for you are before Our eyes; and glorify your Lord with praise when you rise, and in the night, and at the setting of the stars.

keyAyah.why: The question that shook Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim. It leaves three possibilities, and two of them are impossible.

virtues.text: “I heard the Prophet ﷺ reciting al-Ṭūr in the sunset prayer. When he reached this ayah — ‘Or were they created by nothing, or are they the creators? Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they are not certain. Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord, or are they the controllers?’ — my heart almost flew.”
“I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite al-Ṭūr in the sunset prayer.”

before: Al-Dhāriyāt opened with an oath that what you are promised is true, and ended with woe to the disbelievers from their Day. Al-Ṭūr opens with five more oaths that the punishment will fall.
after: Al-Ṭūr ends with glorification “at the setting of the stars”. Al-Najm begins: “By the star when it sets.”
